title: `kubectl`: contexts, namespaces and the declarative workflow

videos.script: kubectl is the one program you will type at for the rest of this course. It is a client, and it needs to know three things: which cluster, as whom, and in which namespace. {{three}} Those three live in one file, and a name for the combination is called a context. Switching clusters is switching contexts. {{context}} Then comes the habit that matters most. You can tell a cluster what to do, one command at a time. Or you can write down what should exist, in a file, and apply it. {{habit}} The second way is called declarative, and this course uses it everywhere. You will see why when a change made by hand shows up as a difference, and the file puts it back. {{drift}}
